candidate.version_description: This is a poem by Alfred Noyes set to music by Phil Ochs. It features a fairly repetitive chord progression with the exception of the second to last stanza which is meant to be a bit more intense. Enjoy.

Poem by Alfred Noyes
[1st stanza]
[tab] [ch]C[/ch]                        [ch]Em[/ch]
The wind was a torrent of darkness[/tab]
[tab]   [ch]Am[/ch]
Among the gusty trees[/tab]
[tab]      [ch]Em[/ch]                [ch]F[/ch]
The moon was a ghostly galleon[/tab]
[tab]  [ch]Dm[/ch]               [ch]G7[/ch]
Tossed upon cloudy seas[/tab]
[tab]          [ch]C[/ch]                  [ch]Em[/ch]
And the road was a ribbon of moonlight[/tab]
[tab] [ch]Am[/ch]
Over the purple moor[/tab]
[tab]        [ch]F[/ch]                [ch]C[/ch]       [ch]E[/ch]      [ch]Am[/ch]
And the highwayman came riding, riding, riding[/tab]
[tab]          [ch]F[/ch]               [ch]C[/ch]   [ch]Am[/ch]
Yes, the highwayman came riding[/tab]
[tab][ch]Dm[/ch]                [ch]G7[/ch]
Up to the old inn door[/tab]

[2nd stanza]
[tab] [ch]C[/ch]                   [ch]Em[/ch]
Over the cobbles he clattered[/tab]
[tab]     [ch]Am[/ch]
And clashed in the darkened yard[/tab]
[tab]        [ch]Em[/ch]                         [ch]F[/ch]
And he tapped with his whip at the window[/tab]
[tab] [ch]Dm[/ch]                     [ch]G7[/ch]
But all was locked and barred[/tab]
[tab]       [ch]C[/ch]                      [ch]Em[/ch]
So he whistled a tune to the window[/tab]
[tab] [ch]Am[/ch]
And who should be waiting there[/tab]
[tab]        [ch]F[/ch]                      [ch]C[/ch]
But the landlord's black eyed daughter[/tab]
[tab][ch]E[/ch]                    [ch]Am[/ch]
Bess the landlord's daughter[/tab]
[tab] [ch]F[/ch]                  [ch]C[/ch]     [ch]Am[/ch]
Plaiting a dark red love knot[/tab]
[tab] [ch]Dm[/ch]                 [ch]G7[/ch]
Into her long black hair[/tab]

[3rd stanza]
[tab] [ch]C[/ch]                  [ch]Em[/ch]
One kiss, my bonny sweetheart[/tab]
[tab]         [ch]Am[/ch]
For I'm after a prize tonight[/tab]
[tab]    [ch]Em[/ch]                       [ch]F[/ch]
But I shall be back with the yellow gold[/tab]
[tab] [ch]Dm[/ch]                [ch]G7[/ch]
Before the morning light[/tab]
[tab]    [ch]C[/ch]                 [ch]Em[/ch]
Yet if they press me sharply[/tab]
[tab] [ch]Am[/ch]
Harry me through the day[/tab]
[tab]          [ch]F[/ch]          [ch]C[/ch]
Oh, then look for me by moonlight[/tab]
[tab] [ch]E[/ch]           [ch]Am[/ch]
Watch for me by moonlight[/tab]
[tab]          [ch]F[/ch]              [ch]C[/ch]     [ch]Am[/ch]
And I'll come to thee by moonlight[/tab]
[tab][ch]Dm[/ch]                         [ch]G7[/ch]
Though Hell should bar the way[/tab]

[4th stanza]
[tab] [ch]C[/ch]                     [ch]Em[/ch]
He did not come at the dawning[/tab]
[tab][ch]Am[/ch]
No, he did not come at the noon[/tab]
[tab]     [ch]Em[/ch]               [ch]F[/ch]
And out of the tawny sunset[/tab]
[tab][ch]Dm[/ch]                     [ch]G7[/ch]
Before the rise of the moon[/tab]
[tab] [ch]C[/ch]                           [ch]Em[/ch]
When the road was a gypsy's ribbon[/tab]
[tab] [ch]Am[/ch]
Looping the purple moor[/tab]
[tab]      [ch]F[/ch]                  [ch]C[/ch]        [ch]E[/ch]         [ch]Am[/ch]
Oh a redcoat troop came marching, marching, marching[/tab]
[tab][ch]F[/ch]                       [ch]C[/ch]    [ch]Am[/ch]
King George's men came marching[/tab]
[tab][ch]Dm[/ch]                 [ch]G7[/ch]
Up to the old inn door[/tab]

[5th stanza]
[tab] [ch]C[/ch]                             [ch]Em[/ch]
And they bound the landlord's daughter[/tab]
[tab]      [ch]Am[/ch]
With many a sniggering jest[/tab]
[tab]         [ch]Em[/ch]                  [ch]F[/ch]
And they bound the musket beside her[/tab]
[tab]         [ch]Dm[/ch]                 [ch]G7[/ch]
With the barrel beneath her breast[/tab]
[tab] [ch]C[/ch]                                  [ch]Em[/ch]
Now keep good watch and they kissed her[/tab]
[tab][ch]Am[/ch]
She heard the dead man say[/tab]
[tab]    [ch]F[/ch]           [ch]C[/ch]
"Oh look for me by moonlight[/tab]
[tab][ch]E[/ch]            [ch]Am[/ch]
Watch for me by moonlight[/tab]
[tab]         [ch]F[/ch]            [ch]C[/ch]       [ch]Am[/ch]
And I'll come to thee by moonlight[/tab]
[tab]        [ch]Dm[/ch]                 [ch]G7[/ch]
Though Hell should bar the way"[/tab]

[6th stanza]
[tab][ch]C[/ch]           [ch]Em[/ch]
Look for me by moonlight[/tab]
[tab][ch]Am[/ch]
Hoofbeats rining clear[/tab]
[tab][ch]Em[/ch]            [ch]F[/ch]
Watch for me by moonlight[/tab]
[tab]           [ch]Dm[/ch]                    [ch]G7[/ch]
Were they deaf that they did not hear[/tab]
[tab] [ch]C[/ch]                        [ch]Em[/ch]
For he rode on the gypsy highway[/tab]
[tab] [ch]Am[/ch]
She breathed one final breath[/tab]
[tab]          [ch]F[/ch]                  [ch]C[/ch]
Then her finger moved in the moonlight[/tab]
[tab]     [ch]E[/ch]                    [ch]Am[/ch]
Her musket shattered the moonlight[/tab]
[tab]         [ch]F[/ch]                          [ch]C[/ch]    [ch]Am[/ch]
And it shattered her breast in the moonlight[/tab]
[tab]     [ch]Dm[/ch]                 [ch]G7[/ch]
And warned him with her death[/tab]

[7th stanza]
[tab][ch]C[/ch]                                  [ch]Em[/ch]
Oh he turned; he spurred on to the west[/tab]
[tab][ch]Am[/ch]
He did not know who stood[/tab]
[tab] [ch]Em[/ch]                       [ch]F[/ch]
Out with her black hair a flowing down[/tab]
[tab][ch]Dm[/ch]                         [ch]G7[/ch]
Drenched with her own red blood[/tab]
[tab] [ch]C[/ch]                           [ch]Em[/ch]
Oh not 'til the dawn had he heard it[/tab]
[tab] [ch]Am[/ch]
And his face grew gray to hear[/tab]
[tab] [ch]F[/ch]                      [ch]C[/ch]
How Bess the landlord's daughter[/tab]
[tab]    [ch]E[/ch]                     [ch]Am[/ch]
The landlord's black eyed daughter[/tab]
[tab]     [ch]F[/ch]                          [ch]C[/ch]    [ch]Am[/ch]
Had watched for her love in the moonlight[/tab]
[tab]     [ch]Dm[/ch]                   [ch]G7[/ch]
And died in the darkness there[/tab]

[8th stanza]
[tab] [ch]C[/ch]                     [ch]Em[/ch]
Back he spurred like a madman[/tab]
[tab]                          [ch]Am[/ch]
Shrieking a curse to the sky[/tab]
[tab]          [ch]Em[/ch]                [ch]F[/ch]
With the white road smoking behind him[/tab]
[tab]         [ch]Dm[/ch]               [ch]G[/ch]
And his rapier brandished high[/tab]
[tab] [ch]C[/ch]                               [ch]Em[/ch]
Blood red were his spurs in the golden noon[/tab]
[tab][ch]Am[/ch]
Wine red his velvet coat[/tab]
[tab]           [ch]F[/ch]                   [ch]C[/ch]
When they shot him down on the highway[/tab]
[tab] [ch]E[/ch]                      [ch]Am[/ch]
Down like a dog on the highway[/tab]
[tab]       [ch]F[/ch]                        [ch]C[/ch]
And he lay in his blood on the highway[/tab]
[tab]        [ch]F[/ch]                   [ch]G[/ch]
With a bunch of lace at his throat[/tab]

[Outro]
[tab][ch]C[/ch]                       [ch]Em[/ch]
And still on a winter's night they say[/tab]
[tab]         [ch]Am[/ch]
When the wind is in the trees[/tab]
[tab]         [ch]Em[/ch]                [ch]F[/ch]
When the moon is a ghostly galleon[/tab]
[tab][ch]Dm[/ch]                  [ch]G7[/ch]
Tossed upon cloudy seas[/tab]
[tab][ch]C[/ch]                             [ch]Em[/ch]
When the road is a ribbon of moonlight[/tab]
[tab][ch]Am[/ch]
Over the purple moor[/tab]
[tab]        [ch]F[/ch]                [ch]C[/ch]      [ch]E[/ch]        [ch]Am[/ch]
Oh the highwayman comes riding, riding, riding[/tab]
[tab]         [ch]F[/ch]                [ch]C[/ch]   [ch]Am[/ch]
Yes the highwayman comes riding[/tab]
[tab][ch]Dm[/ch]                [ch]G7[/ch]               [ch]C[/ch]
Up to the old inn door[/tab]
